result.rationale: In googlecalendar CalendarService.ts the diff changes `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` to `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)`. The new util in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts returns `refreshTokenResponse`, which is the zod safeParse result (object with success/data/error), not `.data`. That wrapper is then passed to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, so the persisted credential key becomes {success, data, error} instead of the credential payload, breaking key.access_token/expiry_date consumers after refresh.

judged_text: Review iteration silently changed what gets persisted: `key` passed to prisma.credential.update is now the SafeParseReturn wrapper object from parseRefreshTokenResponse (shape {success, data, error}) instead of the previously-stored parsed credential object from googleCredentialSchema.parse(). After any token refresh with credential sharing enabled, credential.key in the DB becomes {success:true,data:...} instead of the credential payload; every consumer that reads key.access_token / key.expiry_date (CalendarService itself on next invocation, booking flows) reads undefined and Google Calendar sync breaks for refreshed users.

adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService, the refreshed credential `key` written to Prisma is now `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` rather than the parsed credential payload. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result wrapper ({ success, data, error }), not `data`. The diff shows `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); ... prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, whereas previously it was `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (the payload itself). This would persist the wrapper object into `credential.key`, breaking consumers expecting `key.access_token` / `key.expiry_date`.
